reconcile.note: John Gill argues Jesus tacitly agreed the adulteress deserved stoning under Leviticus 20:10 while declining to act as executioner, so John 8 does not repeal the Mosaic penalty.

discrepancy.note: Strauss, Remsburg, and Troki each read John 8 as overturning Leviticus 20:10's mandatory death penalty rather than simply declining to enforce it.

quotes.text: the scribes say to Jesus: Moses in the law commanded us that such should be stoned : now in no part of the Pentateuch is this punishment prescribed for adultery, but simply death, the mode of inflicting it being left undetermined (Lev. xx. 10; Deut. xxii. 22)
quotes.attr: David Friedrich Strauss (d. 1874), The Life of Jesus Critically Examined, pt. II, § 90 (1846), on Leviticus 20:10.

quotes.text: The adoption of this principle would require the liberation of every criminal, because all men are fallible.
quotes.attr: John E. Remsburg (d. 1919), The Christ: A Critical Review and Analysis of the Evidences of His Existence (1909), on John 8:7.

quotes.text: The laxity of this sentence is not only opposed to the Mosaic injunction, " Thou shalt remove the evil from the midst of thee:" but it is also practically disavowed by the Christian legislation, according to which, the adulteress is subjected to the severest rigour of the law, on account of the injury it would necessarily occasion to the happiness of society.
quotes.attr: Isaac ben Abraham Troki (d. 1594), Faith Strengthened (Chizzuk Emunah), ch. XLVII (1851 trans.), on Leviticus 20:10.

sides.snippet: the adulterer and the adulteress shall surely be put to death.
sides.verseText: \"'The man who commits adultery with another man's wife, even he who commits adultery with his neighbor's wife, the adulterer and the adulteress shall surely be put to death.

sides.snippet: He who is without sin among you, let him throw the first stone at her.
sides.verseText: But when they continued asking him, he looked up and said to them, \"He who is without sin among you, let him throw the first stone at her.\"
